phir-bhi-ye-mol.source: फिर भी ये मोल मैं ना जुटा पाऊँगा
phir-bhi-ye-mol.roman: phir bhī ye mol maiṁ nā juṭā pāūṅgā
phir-bhi-ye-mol.english: {0,1:even then,}{4: I}{5,6,7: will not be able to gather}{2: this }{3:price}
phir-bhi-ye-mol.grammarNote: 'phir bhī' correlates with 'kitnā bhī'. 'juṭā pāūṅgā' is a potential compound verb (juṭānā + pānā) in the 1sg future.

line-01-jai.source: श्री सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईंनाथ महाराज की जय
line-01-jai.roman: Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja kī jaya
line-01-jai.grammarNote: Feminine genitive postposition kī agrees with feminine noun jaya in the conventional celebratory formula.

words.gloss: please take; please do (polite precative auxiliary)

line-03-sun-lije-arji.grammarNote: Compound verb suna līje combines main verb stem sun- with polite precative auxiliary lenā (līje); hamārī agrees in feminine singular with arajī.

line-07-daya-karo.source: दया करो दे दो बाबा कृपा की छाया
line-07-daya-karo.roman: Dayā karo de do bābā kṛpā kī chāyā
line-07-daya-karo.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative clauses: dayā karo and compound imperative de do; kī agrees in feminine singular with chāyā.

line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.source: तुका कहे सेवा मेरी भोली भावड़ी
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.roman: Tukā kahe sevā merī bholī bhāvaḍī
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.grammarNote: Tukā kahe is the standard third-person singular signature formula; merī, bholī, and bhāvaḍī all agree in feminine singular with sevā.

line-10-utho-panduranga.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग प्रभात समय आ गया
line-10-utho-panduranga.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga prabhāta samaya ā gayā

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-10-utho-panduranga.grammarNote: Uṭho is an imperative second-person plural/honorific; ā gayā is a compound verb (ā- + gayā) expressing completed arrival with masculine subject samaya.

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.source: वैष्णवों का मेला गरुड़ पार आ गया
line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.roman: Vaiṣṇavoṁ kā melā Garuḍa Pāra ā gayā

words.gloss: of Vaishnavas; of devotees of Vishnu

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.grammarNote: Garuḍa Pāra is an unmarked locative goal of motion; melā is masculine singular governing the compound verb ā gayā.

line-12-garuda-par-se.source: गरुड़ पार से महाद्वार देहरी तक
line-12-garuda-par-se.roman: Garuḍa Pāra se mahādvāra deharī taka
line-12-garuda-par-se.english: {2:From }{0:the Garuda }{1:platform }{5:up to }{4:the threshold }{3:of the main gate,}
line-12-garuda-par-se.grammarNote: Ablative se paired with inclusive postposition taka establishes a continuous spatial corridor between two temple landmarks.

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.source: शुक सनकादिक नारद तुम्बर भक्त हैं कोटि
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.roman: Śuka Sanakādika Nārada Tumbara bhakta haiṁ koṭi
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.english: {0:Shuka, }{1:Sanaka and the sages, }{2:Narada, }{3:Tumburu, }{6:and crores }{4:of devotees }{5:are present.}

words.gloss: the enlightened sage son of Vyasa

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.grammarNote: A list of proper nouns acting as plural subject governing the plural auxiliary haiṁ; koṭi functions as a post-nominal numeral quantifier modifying bhakta.

line-15-trishula-damaru.source: त्रिशूल डमरू लेकर आये गिरिजा के पति
line-15-trishula-damaru.roman: Triśūla ḍamarū lekara āye Girijā ke pati

words.gloss: small hourglass drum associated with Śiva

line-15-trishula-damaru.grammarNote: Lekara is a conjunctive participle ('having taken'); āye is plural/honorific masculine agreeing with the subject Girijā ke pati.

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.source: कलियुग का भक्त नामा बना कीर्तनी
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.roman: Kaliyuga kā bhakta Nāmā banā kīrtanī
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.english: {3:Nama, }{2:the devotee }{0,1:of the Kali age, }{4:has become }{5:the lead singer of praise,}

words.gloss: kirtan singer; lead performer of holy song

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.grammarNote: Kaliyuga kā bhakta modifies Nāmā in apposition; banā is a simple past/perfective verb governing predicate noun kīrtanī.

line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.source: पीठ पीछे खड़ी आके बन्दगी ये जनी
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.roman: Pīṭha pīche khaḍī āke bandagī ye Janī
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.english: {2:Standing }{0,1:right behind his back, }{5:this }{6:Jani }{3:has come }{4:in humble homage.}
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.grammarNote: Pīṭha pīche is a locative phrase; khaḍī is feminine singular agreeing with Janī; āke is a conjunctive participle.

line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.source: उठो उठो श्री साईंनाथ गुरु चरण कमल दिखलाओ
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.roman: Uṭho uṭho Śrī Sāīnātha guru caraṇa kamala dikhalāo
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative uṭho uṭho shows heightened urgency; caraṇa kamala is a karmadhāraya compound functioning as direct object of causative imperative dikhalāo.

line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.source: फिर भी अज्ञान सी छाई है तुम्हरी योग माया
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.roman: Phira bhī ajñāna sī chāī hai tumharī yoga māyā
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.grammarNote: Compound phrase 'yoga māyā' acts as the feminine singular subject agreeing with 'chāī hai'; 'ajñāna sī' is an adjectival modifier of state.

line-24-bho-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative structure: 'Bho' introduces the titles; 'bhavatimiranāśaka' is a Sanskrit tatpuruṣa compound (bhava + timira + nāśaka) modifying 'ravi'.

line-32-uthakar-netra.source: उठाकर नेत्र पलकें दीन बन्धु रमाकान्ता
line-32-uthakar-netra.roman: Uṭhākara netra palakeṁ dīna bandhu Ramākāntā
line-32-uthakar-netra.english: {0:Lifting }{2:the eyelids }{1:of Your eyes, }{4:O friend }{3:of the humble, }{5:O beloved of Lakshmi,}

words.gloss: beloved of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī, as fortune and splendour; Lord Viṣṇu

line-32-uthakar-netra.grammarNote: 'uṭhākara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on 'dekho' in line 33; 'dīna bandhu' and 'Ramākāntā' are vocative epithets.

line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.source: सुनाओ मधुर वाणी हरो ताप साईंनाथा
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.roman: Sunāo madhura vāṇī haro tāpa Sāīnāthā
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative verbs 'sunāo' and 'haro' addressed to the vocative 'Sāīnāthā'.

line-36-sahan-karke-aao.source: सहन करके आओ चाहे भेट कृष्ण देवा
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.roman: Sahana karake āo cāhe bheṭa Kṛṣṇa devā
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.english: {0,1:bearing it patiently, }{2:come forth; }{3:one longs for }{4:a meeting, }{6:O Lord }{5:Krishna!}
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.grammarNote: 'sahana karake' is a conjunctive participle modifying 'āo'; 'cāhe bheṭa' has an inverted word order with implied subject ('the world/devotee desires a meeting').

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग अब तो दर्शन दो सबको
line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga aba to darśana do sabako

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.grammarNote: Coordinate imperatives 'uṭho' and 'do'; 'Pāṇḍuraṅga' is vocative; 'to' adds emphatic pleading.

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.source: राई रखुमाबाई मन में आने दो दया
line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.roman: Rāī Rakhumābaī mana meṁ āne do dayā

words.gloss: Rakhumābāī, Rukmiṇī the gold-adorned goddess; consort of Viṭṭhala

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.grammarNote: Vocative direct address 'Rāī Rakhumābaī' governing permissive verbal construction 'āne do' with direct object 'dayā'.

words.gloss: Hanumān, the one with prominent jaws; Rāma’s divine attendant and devotee

line-45-garuda-hanumanta-thade.grammarNote: Plural subject 'Garuḍa Hanumanta' takes the stative participle 'ṭhāḍe' and imperfective verb 'johate'; 'bāṭa' is the accusative complement of the idiom.

line-48-vishnudasa-nama-khada.grammarNote: Appositive proper noun 'Viṣṇudāsa Nāmā' is the subject of the predicate adjective 'khaḍā' with conjunctive participle phrase 'lekara kākaḍā'.

line-49-lekar-pancharati.source: लेकर पञ्चारती करूँ बाबा की आरती
line-49-lekar-pancharati.roman: Lekara pañcāratī karūṁ bābā kī āratī
line-49-lekar-pancharati.english: {0:Holding }{1:the five-flame lamp, }{2:I offer }{5:worship with lights }{3,4:to Baba.}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-49-lekar-pancharati.grammarNote: First person singular verb 'karūṁ' taking 'āratī' as direct object; 'pañcāratī' is governed by 'lekara'.

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.source: उठो उठो हे बान्धव मनाओ ये रमाधव
line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.roman: Uṭho uṭho he bāndhava manāo ye Ramādhava

words.gloss: Ramādhava, husband of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī who embodies fortune and splendour; Viṣṇu

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative 'uṭho uṭho' for devotional emphasis; vocative 'he bāndhava'; second-person plural imperative 'manāo'.

line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.source: कृष्णनाथा दत्त साई पदों में चित्त जड़े साई
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.roman: Kṛṣṇanāthā Datta Sāī padoṁ meṁ citta jaḍe Sāī
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.english: {0:Krishnanatha }{6:fixes }{5:his consciousness }{3,4:at the feet }{1,2:of Datta Sai, }{7:O Sai.}
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.grammarNote: Subject 'Kṛṣṇanāthā' with transitive verb 'jaḍe' (3rd person singular present in poetic Hindi); 'Sāī' is repeated at the end for rhythmic emphasis.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-53-kakada-arati-karata.grammarNote: Participle 'karatā' used as finite present verb with implicit first-person subject; 'Sāīnātha devā' is in the vocative case.

line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.source: साईंनाथ के भक्ति ताप से उसको जलाया
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.roman: Sāīnātha ke bhakti tāpa se usako jalāyā
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.grammarNote: Causative/transitive past verb 'jalāyā' taking pronoun 'usako' as direct object; 'bhakti tāpa se' is the instrumental cause.

line-61-aise-datta-deva.source: ऐसे दत्त देव शिरडी रहकर भी मिलते
line-61-aise-datta-deva.roman: Aise Datta deva Śiraḍī rahakar bhī milate
line-61-aise-datta-deva.english: {0:In such a way} {1,2:Lord Datta} {6:meets seekers,} {4,5:even while dwelling} {3:in Shirdi.}

words.gloss: Shirdi (the sacred village of Sai Baba)

line-61-aise-datta-deva.grammarNote: Aise functions adverbially modifying milate. Rahakar is a conjunctive participle (rah- + kar) expressing simultaneous or attendant circumstance.

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.source: सगुण दर्शन पाने जन जन शिरडी आ रहा
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.roman: Saguṇa darśana pāne jana jana Śiraḍī ā rahā
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.english: {2:To obtain} {1:the sacred vision} {0:of your embodied form,} {3,4:multitudes of people} {6,7:are coming} {5:to Shirdi.}

words.gloss: with manifest attributes; embodied divine form

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.grammarNote: Pāne is the oblique infinitive of purpose. Jana jana is a distributive reduplication functioning as a singular collective subject with masculine singular agreement in ā rahā.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
I wave in offering; I circle

line-72-arati-utaru-mere.grammarNote: Paṇḍharīnāthā is in the vocative case (Paṇḍharīnātha + ā extension common in devotional Marathi/Hindi verse).

line-73-mere-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative phrase standing in direct apposition to Paṇḍharīnāthā in line 72.

line-80-inta-para-khada.source: ईंट पर खड़ा हुआ है सुन्दर बाबा
line-80-inta-para-khada.roman: Ī̃ṭa para khaḍā huā hai sundara bābā

words.gloss: brick (the sacred brick thrown by Pundalik)

line-80-inta-para-khada.grammarNote: Ī̃ṭa para is a locative postpositional phrase. Khaḍā huā hai is a stative periphrastic construction agreeing with the masculine subject sundara bābā.

line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.source: उठकर भोर में बाबा खड़े हैं ईंट पे
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.roman: Uṭhakara bhora meṁ bābā khaḍe haiṁ ī̃ṭa pe
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle 'uṭhakara' preceding the main predicate 'khaḍe haiṁ'. Honorific plural verb 'haiṁ' and participle 'khaḍe' with singular subject 'bābā'. Postposition 'pe' is a colloquial variant of 'par'.

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.source: केशवराज ईंट पे खड़े नामा चरण पूजते
line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.roman: Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe Nāmā caraṇa pūjate

words.gloss: King Keśava, the fine-haired lord, here Viṭṭhala

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.grammarNote: Two balanced clauses combined in one line: 'Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe [haiṁ]' and 'Nāmā caraṇa pūjate [haiṁ]'. 'Nāmā' refers to the Marathi saint-poet Namdev.

line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.source: साईंनाथ गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.roman: Sāīnātha guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Sainath, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sai.}
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: Vocative titles 'Sāīnātha', 'guru merī māī', and 'Sāī'. 'De do' is a compound verb (stem 'de' + vector verb 'do') forming a polite/pleading imperative. 'Caraṇoṁ' is the oblique plural of 'caraṇa'.

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.source: दत्तराज गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.roman: Dattarāja guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Dattaraja, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sai.}

words.gloss: King Datta, the given one; Lord Dattātreya

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: 'Dattarāja' is a tatpuruṣa/karmadhāraya title (Datta + rāja). Syntax and verbal morphology identical to line 93.

verse-3-1.source: दान धर्म से मोह है घटता यह बतलाने आये
verse-3-1.roman: dān dharm se moh hai ghaṭtā yah batlāne āye

words.gloss: right order, duty, or sustaining principle
to explain; to teach; to show

verse-3-1.grammarNote: `dān dharm se moh hai ghaṭtā` is an embedded declarative clause functioning as the antecedent of `yah`. `batlāne` is an oblique infinitive of purpose governing `āye`.

line-000.source: श्री सच्चिदानंद सद्गुरु साईनाथ महाराज की जय
line-000.roman: Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja kī jaya
line-000.grammarNote: Standard Hindi/Marathi jaikāra formula; 'kī' is the feminine genitive postposition agreeing with feminine noun 'jaya'.

line-001.source: ओवाळू आरती माझ्या सद्गुरुनाथा माझ्या साईनाथा
line-001.roman: Ovāḷū āratī mājhyā sadgurunāthā mājhyā sāīnāthā
line-001.english: {0:Let me wave }{1:the āratī }{2:before my }{3:Sadguru Lord, }{4:my }{5:Lord Sai.}

words.gloss: let me wave in circle; I wave
ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
unto the true teacher and master

line-001.grammarNote: Ovāḷū is the 1st person singular optative/present of ovāḷaṇe; 'sadgurunāthā' and 'sāīnāthā' take the oblique/dative vocative marker -ā.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-013.grammarNote: Jñānarājā is vocative/dative formed from jñāna + rājā.

line-019.grammarNote: Brahmaci has the emphatic enclitic -ci ('verily / alone'); kēlē is neuter singular past agreeing with viśva.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-025.grammarNote: Dhāmā is vocative singular form of dhāma.

line-031.grammarNote: Abhaṅga is neuter plural; rakṣilē is neuter plural past participle.

line-033.grammarNote: Brahma is neuter singular subject; ālē is neuter past participle; Tukāsī has the dative/objective suffix -sī.

line-037.source: आळवितो सप्रेमे तुजला आरती घेउन करी हो
line-037.roman: Āḷavitō saprēmē tujalā āratī ghēuna karī hō

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-037.grammarNote: Āḷavitō is 1st person masculine present of āḷavaṇe; ghēuna is absolutive participle ('having taken'); karī is locative singular/plural.

line-052.source: आळवितो सप्रेमे तुजला आरती घेवून करी हो
line-052.roman: āḷavito sapreme tujalā āratī gheūna karī ho

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-052.grammarNote: āḷavito from āḷavaṇē ('to invoke, sing plaintively'). karī is locative singular of kara ('hand').

line-067.grammarNote: Standard Hindi/Marathi victory formula: [Name/Title] + kī jaya ('victory to...').

line-069.source: पाहे प्रसादाची वाट द्यावे धुवोनिया ताट
line-069.roman: pāhe prasādācī vāṭa dyāve dhuvoniyā tāṭa
line-069.english: {0,2:[I] await }{1:the prasad; }{4:having washed }{5:the dining plate, }{3:please give it.}
line-069.grammarNote: pāhe vāṭa is an idiomatic light verb construction ('awaits'). dhuvoniyā is an archaic Marathi conjunctive participle ('having washed').

line-073.source: पावला प्रसाद आता उठोनि जावे बाबा आता निजवे
line-073.roman: pāvalā prasāda ātā uṭhoni jāve bābā ātā nijave
line-073.english: {1:The prasad }{0:is received; }{2:now, }{3:rising, }{4:one should depart, }{5:O Baba, }{6:now }{7:please rest.}

words.gloss: one should go; we shall leave

line-073.grammarNote: jāve and nijave are impersonal potential/optative verb forms used as polite imperatives. pāvalā agrees with masculine prasāda.

line-175.english: {3,4:Every single day}{1: taking bath}{2: and reciting japa}{0: in Kashi,}
line-175.grammarNote: Elliptical nominal phrase describing Dattatreya's daily spiritual routine.

line-182.source: कमंडलु मृगछाला धारित है सिर पे
line-182.roman: kamaṇḍalu mṛgachālā dhārita hai sira pe
line-182.english: {0:A water-pot}{1: and deerskin}{2,3: donned,}{4,5: and on your head}
line-182.grammarNote: Passive/attributive construction with locative 'sira pe' continuing into the next line.

line-000.source: श्री सच्चिदानंद सद्गुरू साईनाथ महाराज की जय
line-000.roman: Śrī saccidānanda sadgurū sāīnātha mahārāja kī jaya

line-pahacha-8-m.source: ଅଷ୍ଟମେ ଗୁହାରି କଲି କାଟ ଅଷ୍ଟପାଶ / ମାୟାପୀଡ଼ିତ ଭକ୍ତର ଆହେ ଅବିନାଶ
line-pahacha-8-m.roman: aṣṭame guhāri kali kāṭa aṣṭapāśa / māyāpīṛita bhaktara āhe abināśa
line-pahacha-8-m.english: {0:On the eighth,}{2: I made}{1: an earnest plea:}{3: sever}{4: the eight bonds}{6: of the devotee}{5: afflicted by māyā,}{7: O}{8: Imperishable One.}
line-pahacha-8-m.grammarNote: Identical syntax and morphemes to line-pahacha-8-f.

line-pahacha-9.source: ନବମ ପାହାଚେ ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ନବଗ୍ରହ / ଯୋଡ଼ହସ୍ତେ ଛନ୍ତି ଠିଆ ଚାହିଁ ତୁମ ମୁହଁ
line-pahacha-9.roman: nabama pāhāce dṛśya hele nabagraha / yoṛahaste chanti ṭhiā cāhiṁ tuma muhaṁ
line-pahacha-9.english: {0:On the ninth}{1: step,}{4: the nine planets}{3: became}{2: visible;}{6: they are}{7: standing}{5: with folded hands,}{8: gazing upon}{9: your}{10: face.}
line-pahacha-9.grammarNote: nabagraha is the plural subject. hele is 3rd person plural past auxiliary. chanti ṭhiā is a present progressive verbal phrase ('are standing'). cāhiṁ is a conjunctive participle.

line-pahacha-16.source: ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ପାହାଚେ ମାତା ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ଦେବୀଙ୍କୁ / ସ୍ମରିଲି ସୃଷ୍ଟିର ମୂଳ ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ଶକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ
line-pahacha-16.roman: ṣoṛaśa pāhāce mātā ṣoṛaśa debīṅku / smarili sṛṣṭira mūḷa ṣoṛaśa śaktiṅku
line-pahacha-16.english: {0:On the sixteenth}{1: step,}{5: I remembered}{3: the sixteen}{2: Mother}{4: Goddesses,}{8: the sixteen}{7: primal}{9: Shaktis}{6: of creation.}
line-pahacha-16.grammarNote: debīṅku and śaktiṅku carry the plural/honorific accusative suffix -ṅku. sṛṣṭira is genitive singular. smarili is 1st person past indicative.

line-pahacha-19.source: ଉଣେଇଶ ପାହାଚରେ ପତିତପାବନ / ମନ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳ ଅତି ଲଭିବାକୁ ଦର୍ଶନ
line-pahacha-19.roman: uṇe'iśa pāhācare patitapābana / mana byākuḷa ati labhibāku darśana
line-pahacha-19.english: {0:On the nineteenth}{1: step}{2: is Patitapabana;}{3: my heart}{5: is exceedingly}{4: anxious}{6: to attain}{7: darshan.}

words.gloss: sacred sight / vision of the deity

line-pahacha-19.grammarNote: pāhācare is locative. patitapābana stands as the devotional focus. labhibāku is an infinitive of purpose in -bāku governing darśana.

line-pahacha-21.source: ଏକୋଇଶି ପାହାଚେ ପ୍ରଣାମି ଦେବଦେବୀ / ଡାକିଲି ଦର୍ଶନ ଦିଅ ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ ସ୍ୱାମୀ
line-pahacha-21.roman: eko'iśi pāhāce praṇāmī debadebī / ḍākili darśana di'a jagannātha swāmī
line-pahacha-21.english: {0:On the twenty-first}{1: step,}{2: having bowed to}{3: the gods and goddesses,}{4: I called out,}{6: grant}{5: darshan,}{7: O Jagannath}{8: Swami!}
line-pahacha-21.grammarNote: praṇāmī is a non-finite conjunctive participle ('having saluted'). debadebī is a dvandva compound ('gods and goddesses'). ḍākili is 1st person past. di'a is a direct 2nd person imperative.

words.gloss: power of worldly appearance and delusion

main-maya-mein-ghira-bechara.grammarNote: `ghirā` is a past/stative participle from intransitive/passive `ghirnā` ('to be surrounded'), agreeing in masculine singular with `Maĩ`. `bechārā` functions as an appositive descriptive adjective.

verse2-1.source: ବାଜେ ରେ ମହୁରୀ ଖୋଳ କରତାଳ ରଣଶିଙ୍ଗା ଭେରୀ ବାଜା
verse2-1.roman: bāje re mahurī khoḷa karatāḷa raṇaśiṅgā bherī bājā
verse2-1.english: {0:There resound, }{1:O, }{2:the reed pipe, }{3:khol, }{4:cymbals, }{5:battle horn, }{6:kettledrum, }{7:and musical instruments!}
verse2-1.grammarNote: 'bāje' is 3rd person present. The subject is an asyndetic list of traditional musical instruments ending in the collective term 'bājā'.

verse3-1.source: ଯୋଗ ସମାଧିରେ ସାଇ ଯୋଗୀରାଜ ଶୋଇଛନ୍ତି ମନ୍ଦିରରେ
verse3-1.roman: yoga samādhire sāi yogīrāja śoichanti mandirare
verse3-1.english: {0:In yoga }{1:samādhi, }{2:Sai, }{3:the king of yogis, }{4:rests }{5:in the temple.}
verse3-1.grammarNote: 'yoga samādhire' forms a compound concept in the locative case -re. 'śoichanti' is honorific present continuous/stative from 'śoibā'.

verse3-2.source: ପ୍ରତିମା ରୂପରେ ବିରାଜିତ ସାଇ ସମାଧି ମନ୍ଦିର ଘରେ
verse3-2.roman: pratimā rūpare birājita sāi samādhi mandira ghare
verse3-2.english: {1:In the form }{0:of a sculpted image, }{3:Sai }{2:sits resplendent }{6:in the chamber }{4:of the samādhi }{5:temple.}

words.gloss: tomb; here Sāī Bābā’s burial shrine

verse3-2.grammarNote: 'pratimā rūpare' uses the locative of guise/form. 'samādhi mandira ghare' is a genitival compound phrase ending in locative -e.

v1-2.english: {0:Birth}{1: and death}{3: are indeed}{2: the play}{4: of māyā.}

words.gloss: of the power of worldly appearance

v1-2.grammarNote: Janama maraṇa is an asyndetic dvandva compound functioning in apposition to kheḷa. māyāra carries the Odia genitive suffix -ra.

words.gloss: under the sway of māyā (the delusive power of worldly appearance)

v2-4.grammarNote: 'māyābaśe' is a compound noun in locative/adverbial case ('māyā' + 'baśa' + '-e'); 'bāṭabaṇā' is a predicative adjective with copula/inchoative verb 'hue'.

janena-mu-debata-ki.grammarNote: First-person singular present negative verb 'jāṇenā' formed from the verb stem 'jāṇ-' with negative suffix '-nā', followed by 1sg pronoun 'mū̃' and disjunctive interrogative particle 'ki'.

janena-mu-ishwara.english: {0,1:I do not know }{2:if the Supreme Lord,}
janena-mu-ishwara.grammarNote: Repeated 1sg negative clause structure with the Sanskrit loanword 'īśbara' (īśvara) functioning as the predicate noun of the complement clause.

bihuchuna-chakara.grammarNote: Noun adjunct 'biuchuṇā', the sung colloquial form of 'biñcaṇā' (hand-fan), qualifying the agent noun 'cākara'.

words.gloss: power of worldly appearance and entanglement
from the net; from the snare

janamara-maya-jalu.grammarNote: Genitive 'janamara' qualifying the compound 'māyā jāla', which carries the ablative inflection '-u' ('jālu').

words.gloss: right order, duty, or sustaining principle

dharama-karama-nija-swarthare.grammarNote: Asyndetic compound 'Dharama karama' (semi-tatsama forms of dharma and karma); 'swārthare' has locative/instrumental suffix '-re' expressing purpose/motive.

refrain-luha-bohi-jae.source: ଲୁହ ବହି ଯାଏ ତୁମ ଶ୍ରୀମୁଖ ଦରଶନେ
refrain-luha-bohi-jae.roman: luha bahi yāē tuma śrīmukha daraśanē
refrain-luha-bohi-jae.english: {0:Tears}{1,2: stream forth}{5: at the sight of}{3: your}{4: holy face}

words.gloss: at the sight of; upon beholding

refrain-luha-bohi-jae.grammarNote: Compound verb `bahi yāē` (conjunctive participle + 3rd person present auxiliary). `daraśanē` is a locative of circumstance / temporal cause (`daraśana` + `-ē`).

refrain-deha-thari-uthe.source: ଦେହ ଥରି ଉଠେ ତୁମ ପାବନ ପରଶେ
refrain-deha-thari-uthe.roman: dēha thari uṭhē tuma pābana paraśē
refrain-deha-thari-uthe.english: {0:The body}{2: starts }{1:trembling}{3: at your}{4: purifying}{5: touch}
refrain-deha-thari-uthe.grammarNote: Ingressive compound verb `thari uṭhē` (`thari` + `uṭhē` 3rd person simple present). `paraśē` is locative of cause (from `paraśa` / Sanskrit `sparśa`).

refrain-antare-jaage-je.source: ଅନ୍ତରେ ଜାଗେ ଯେ କୋହ ଶୁଣି ତୁମ ଗୀତ
refrain-antare-jaage-je.roman: antarē jāgē yē kōha śuṇi tuma gīta
refrain-antare-jaage-je.english: {0:Within,}{3: a choked sob}{1,2: awakens}{4: upon hearing}{5: your}{6: song}
refrain-antare-jaage-je.grammarNote: `śuṇi` is a non-finite conjunctive participle taking `tuma gīta` as its object. `yē` functions as an emphatic or relative connector.

refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.source: ପ୍ରାଣ ପୁଲକିତ ହୁଏ ତୁମ ସାଈ ନାମେ
refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.roman: prāṇa pulakita huē tuma sāī nāmē
refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.english: {0:The life-breath}{1,2: is thrilled}{3: by your}{4: Sai}{5: name}
refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.grammarNote: `pulakita huē` is a predicate adjective construction with copular verb `huē` (3rd person present). `nāmē` is an instrumental/locative of cause.

v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.source: ଭକତି ଯେ ବ୍ୟଥା ଦିଏ ନଥିଲି ମୁଁ ଜାଣି
v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.roman: bhakati yē byathā diē nathilī mū̃ jāṇi
v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.english: {1:That}{0: devotion}{3: gives}{2: pain,}{5: I}{4: did not}{6: know}
v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.grammarNote: Inverted word order in main clause: negative auxiliary `nathilī` precedes subject `mū̃` and lexical participle `jāṇi` (`nathilī mū̃ jāṇi` for standard `mū̃ jāṇi nathilī`). `yē` introduces the subordinate content clause.

v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.source: ତମକୁ ଲୋଡୁଛି ମୁଁ ଯେ ପ୍ରତି ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତରେ
v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.roman: tamaku lōḍuchi mū̃ yē prati muhūrttarē
v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.english: {2:I}{1: am seeking}{0: you}{3: indeed}{4: at every}{5: moment}
v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.grammarNote: Inverted word order: Object (`tamaku`) - Verb (`lōḍuchi` 1st person present continuous) - Subject (`mū̃`) - Particle (`yē`). `muhūrttarē` is locative of time.

v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.source: ସ୍ନେହ ପ୍ରେମ ରାଗ ପ୍ରୀତି ସଉରାଗଠୁ ବେଶୀ
v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.roman: snēha prēma rāga prīti saurāgaṭhu bēśī
v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.english: {0:Affection,}{1: love,}{2: passion,}{3: fondness—}{5:more}{4: than passionate yearning}

words.gloss: than passionate yearning; beyond deep love

v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.grammarNote: Asyndetic listing of four terms for love (`snēha`, `prēma`, `rāga`, `prīti`). `saurāgaṭhu` carries the ablative-comparative suffix `-ṭhu` governing `bēśī`.

v1-karunara-bhaba-jhare.english: {1:The feeling}{0: of compassion}{2: streams}{3: from your very}{4: eyes}

words.gloss: in the eyes; from the eyes

v1-karunara-bhaba-jhare.grammarNote: `jharē` is 3rd person simple present. `tumari` has the emphatic clitic `-i`. `nayanē` is a locative noun functioning with ablative/source meaning.

v2-janama-marana-die.grammarNote: Inverted word order: Object dvandva (`janama maraṇa`) - Verb (`diē` 3rd person present) - Subject (`niṣṭhura samaya`).

v2-mo-aatmare-naahi-kintu.source: ମୋ ଆତ୍ମାରେ ନାହିଁ କିନ୍ତୁ ତୁମରି ବିଲୟ
v2-mo-aatmare-naahi-kintu.roman: mō ātmārē nāhī̃ kintu tumari bilaya
v2-mo-aatmare-naahi-kintu.english: {3:But}{0,1: in my soul,}{2: there is no}{5: dissolution}{4: of you}

words.gloss: in the soul; within the self

v2-mo-aatmare-naahi-kintu.grammarNote: `nāhī̃` is the negative existential copula. `tumari` carries emphatic `-i` indicating 'of you alone'.

v2-kete-janma-pare-aaba.source: କେତେ ଜନ୍ମ ପରେ ଅବା କେତେ କଳ୍ପ ପରେ
v2-kete-janma-pare-aaba.roman: kētē janma parē abā kētē kalpa parē
v2-kete-janma-pare-aaba.english: {2:After}{0: so many}{1: births,}{3: or}{6: after}{4: so many}{5: aeons,}
v2-kete-janma-pare-aaba.grammarNote: Parallel temporal postpositional phrases coordinated by the disjunctive marker `abā`.

v2-mo-aatmare-thiba-tume.source: ମୋ ଆତ୍ମାରେ ଥିବ ତୁମେ ଆହେ ଦୟାମୟ
v2-mo-aatmare-thiba-tume.roman: mō ātmārē thiba tumē āhē dayāmaya
v2-mo-aatmare-thiba-tume.english: {3:You}{2: will abide}{0,1: in my soul,}{4: O}{5: Merciful One}

words.gloss: in the soul; within my self

v2-mo-aatmare-thiba-tume.grammarNote: Inverted clause structure: Locative (`mō ātmārē`) - Verb (`thiba` 2nd/3rd person future/continuative) - Subject (`tumē`) - Vocative phrase (`āhē dayāmaya`).

verse-5-line-1.source: ତୁମରି ସମାଧି ନିକଟେ ଗୁରୁ ହେ ସଭିଏଁ କରନ୍ତି ଆଳି
verse-5-line-1.roman: Tumari samādhi nikaṭē guru hē sabhiēṃ karanti āḷi

words.gloss: tomb-shrine / final resting place of yogic absorption
near / beside / in the presence of (locative)

verse-5-line-1.grammarNote: 'Samādhi' is a preserved Vedantic/devotional term denoting both yogic absorption and the shrine housing the master's physical form. 'Sabhiēṃ' is an all-inclusive collective pronoun with plural verb agreement ('karanti').

words.gloss: she who possesses/wields great māyā; cosmic creative power

parvati-devi-mahamayavini.grammarNote: Series of Sanskrit feminine nouns and epithets in apposition: proper noun Pārvatī, title Devī, and possessive compound Mahāmāyāvinī (mahā-māyā + possessive suffix -vinī).

words.gloss: savior of the universe; deliverer who ferries creation across

tuma-shakti-ho-jagatarini.grammarNote: Direct Hindi clause: subject 'Tuma' + predicate noun 'Śakti' + copula 'Ho' + appositive Sanskrit compound epithet 'Jagatāriṇī' (jagat + tāriṇī).

aarti-kijai-shailsuta-ki.english: {0,1:Perform the āratī}{2,3: of the Daughter of the Mountain}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform

aarti-kijai-shailsuta-ki.grammarNote: Old Hindi/Braj honorific passive imperative verb `kījai` governing the accusative/patient noun `āratī`, postmodified by the feminine genitive phrase `śailasutā kī`.

jagadamba-ki-aarti-kijai.english: {2,3:Perform the āratī}{1: of }{0:the Mother of the Universe}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform

jagadamba-ki-aarti-kijai.grammarNote: Preposed feminine genitive modifier `Jagadambā kī` qualifying `āratī`, governed by passive imperative `kījai`.

aarti-kijai-aarti-kijai-shailsuta-ki.source: आरती कीजै आरती कीजै शैलसुता की
aarti-kijai-aarti-kijai-shailsuta-ki.roman: Āratī kījai āratī kījai śailasutā kī
aarti-kijai-aarti-kijai-shailsuta-ki.english: {0,1:Perform the āratī}, {2,3:perform the āratī}{4,5: of the Daughter of the Mountain}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform
ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform

aarti-kijai-aarti-kijai-shailsuta-ki.grammarNote: Reduplicated verb phrase `āratī kījai` for rhythmic and devotional emphasis, completing with the genitive complement `śailasutā kī`.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

kare-aarti-miljul-taki.grammarNote: Verb-initial clause `kare` governing direct object `āratī`, with manner adverb `milajula` and postposed archaic/Braj genitive pronoun `tākī`.

aarti-kijai-x3-shailsuta-ki.source: आरती कीजै आरती कीजै आरती कीजै शैलसुता की
aarti-kijai-x3-shailsuta-ki.roman: Āratī kījai āratī kījai āratī kījai śailasutā kī
aarti-kijai-x3-shailsuta-ki.english: {0,1:Perform the āratī}, {2,3:perform the āratī}, {4,5:perform the āratī}{6,7: of the Daughter of the Mountain}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform
ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform
ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform

aarti-kijai-x3-shailsuta-ki.grammarNote: Threefold reduplication of the imperative verb phrase `āratī kījai` preceding the genitive complement `śailasutā kī`.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
let be performed; one should perform

ki-aarti-kijai.grammarNote: Genitive postposition `kī` linking back to the Devi's name, followed by direct object `āratī` and passive imperative verb `kījai`.

words.gloss: a context-dependent power or condition of worldly appearance

ye-kaisi-tumhaari-maaya-hai.grammarNote: Interrogative pronominal adjective kaisī and possessive pronoun tumhārī agree with feminine singular noun māyā.

verse-2-male.source: कोई उतारे आरती, कोई उतारे आरती, श्री गुरु के चरणों में कोई हँसे कोई रोए रे
verse-2-male.roman: koī utāre āratī, koī utāre āratī, śrī guru ke caraṇoṁ meṁ koī haṁse koī roe re

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

verse-2-male.grammarNote: utāre, haṁse, roe are 3rd pers. sg. habitual/present verb forms; caraṇoṁ meṁ is masculine plural oblique with locative postposition; koī... koī... sets up a contrastive parallel pair.

verse-2-female.source: कोई उतारे आरती, कोई उतारे आरती, श्री गुरु के चरणों में कोई हँसे कोई रोए रे, कोई हँसे कोई रोए रे
verse-2-female.roman: koī utāre āratī, koī utāre āratī, śrī guru ke caraṇoṁ meṁ koī haṁse koī roe re, koī haṁse koī roe re

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

verse-2-female.grammarNote: Repetition of koī haṁse koī roe re concludes the choral line for musical symmetry.

verse-3-male.source: जोगी लिए दर्शन, जोगी लिए दर्शन, साधु चले हो मगन, ये तो गुरु साईं लीला रे
verse-3-male.roman: jogī lie darśana, jogī lie darśana, sādhu cale ho magana, ye to guru sāīṁ līlā re
verse-3-male.grammarNote: lie is perfective participle functioning as present/habitual 'take'; ho magana is conjunctive/adverbial participle phrase modifying cale; to is emphatic particle.

v10-l2.grammarNote: Sandhi breaks across tokens: `muṭi mēl` + `aṇintu` + `eṉ` yields surface tokens `muṭimē` and `laṇinteṉ`. Relative participle `pukunta` modifies causal instrumental pronoun `ataṉāl`. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v10-l3.grammarNote: Aḻivikkum is a causative relative form attached to the full noun phrase aṇṇal tirunīṟu: the Lord’s sacred ash is the effective subject. Cemmai is its goodness or excellence; tiṭamē affirms that this is assured. The three performed occurrences are retained individually.

v10-l4.source: அத்தகு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே

v11-l1.source: தேனமர் பொழில்கொள் ஆலை விளைசெந்நெல் துன்னி வளர்செம்பொன் எங்கும் நிகழ
v11-l1.roman: tēṉamar poḻilkoḷ ālai viḷaicennel tuṉṉi vaḷarcempoṉ eṅkum nikaḻa
v11-l1.english: Amid {0:honey-rich }{1:groves, }{2:sugarcane mills, }and {3:ripening red rice }{4:clustered together, }{5:fine gold abounding }{6:everywhere }{7:in sight,}
v11-l1.grammarNote: Infinitive `nikaḻa` functions adverbially/circumstantially ('as ... shines/manifests'). Compound chain: `tēṉ-amar` (honey-settling), `poḻil-koḷ` (grove-bearing), `viḷai-cem-nel` (ripening-red-paddy), `vaḷar-cem-poṉ` (growing-fine-gold).

v11-l2.source: நான்முகன் ஆதி யாய பிரமா புரத்து மறைஞான ஞான முனிவன்

v11-l2.english: {6:the wise }{7:sage, }{5:versed in Vedic knowledge, }{3,4:of Brahmapuram, }{1,2:which takes its name from }{0:the Four-faced One,}

words.gloss: origin or beginning; here, the origin of the city’s name
being or becoming; linking the origin to Brahmapuram

v11-l2.grammarNote: Nāṉmukaṉ is the Four-faced One. Āti yāya relates the origin of Brahmapuram to him; it does not say that he owns the city. Maṟaiñāṉa gives Vedic knowledge, and ñāṉa qualifies the sage as wise. The English subject is this sage, continued by spoke in the next row.

v11-l3.source: தானுறு கோளும் நாளும் அடியாரை வந்து நலியாத வண்ணம் உரைசெய்
v11-l3.roman: tāṉuṟu kōḷum nāḷum aṭiyārai vantu naliyāta vaṇṇam uraicey
v11-l3.english: {7:spoke }{6:so that }{1:planets }{2:and asterisms, }{0:as they take their course, }{5:may not }{4:come }{5:and afflict }{3:devotees.}

words.gloss: spoke or composed; here, the sage’s utterance that forms the following word-garland

v11-l3.grammarNote: Naliyāta is negative and qualifies vaṇṇam: so that they do not afflict. Uraicey is the utterance/composition expression linked to the following garland of words; do not assert an overt past-tense suffix absent from the supplied form. English uses spoke as a finite clause, then resumes the resulting garland with this in the next sentence.

v11-l4.source: ஆனசொல் மாலை யோதும் அடியார்கள் வானில் அரசாள்வர் ஆணை நமதே
v11-l4.roman: āṉacol mālai yōtum aṭiyārkaḷ vāṉil aracāḷvar āṇai namatē
v11-l4.english: {3:Devotees }{2:who recite }{1:this garland }{0:of potent words }{5:shall reign }{4:in heaven; }{7:this is our }{6:solemn decree!}
v11-l4.grammarNote: Sandhi: `mālai` + `ōtum` -> `mālai yōtum`. Future verb `aracāḷvar` asserts the promised fruit. `āṇai namatē` is an emphatic nominal sentence of sovereign declaration.

v11-closing.grammarNote: Nominal sentence `āṇai namatē` (noun + possessive pronoun with emphatic `-ē`) chanted in fourfold repetition.

l007.grammarNote: Read the previous genitive with these four forms: Viṣṇu’s four vyūhas. The native scholarly note names Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. Those unsung names are explanatory only.

g008.grammarNote: Mān means pride here. The destroying action of mardan continues from the preceding line: the addressed Lord crushes pride. A Punjabi commentary alternatively construes the full phrase as crusher of Madhu’s pride; neither reading identifies a king named Māndhātā.

words.gloss: one who wards off; saves from

editorialAdjustments.reason: The reviewed śabd means words: jewels, weapons, life, shared wealth, and God; śabdeci is with words alone. The poem does not identify those words as divine or teacher names. theme.name_power specifically requires the significance or efficacy of such names, so this classification imports unsupported meaning. Retain offering from the actual honour/worship clause.

g024.grammarNote: Proposed performed phrase of canonical l009 tokens5–9; adjacent actual phrases retain the connected prayer. Three practices are coordinated; the predicate is conditioned by pleasing the Lord, not an unqualified validation of ritual or ascetic display.
